 Fire Risk Prompts BMW to Recall More Than 720,000 Vehicles and Warns Owners to Park Outside
 First for Autos Follow Jennifer Mashuga Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:31 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:31 PM UTC Instagram/BMW Group BMW has announced a major recall covering 720,796 vehicles that could catch fire, even when the engine is off.
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) first announced the recall on Wednesday, November 4, warning that an improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump can let moisture in. That can cause a short circuit and, in turn, a fire. Given the severity of the risk, BMW is urging owners to park affected vehicles "outside and away from structures" until a fix is available.
 The recall covers a wide range of models: 3 Series and 5 Series (2012-2016); 2 Series and 4 Series coupes (2014-2016); 3 Series Sports Wagons (2014-2016); 4 Series convertibles (2014-2016); 2 Series convertibles (2015-2016); 4 Series Gran Coupes (2015-2016); X1 (2012-2015); X3 (2013-2017); X4 (2015-2018); Z4 (2012-2016); X5 xDrive40e (2016-2018); and the 328xi Gran Turismo (2014-2016).
 Instagram/BMW Group
 This isn't the first time BMW has dealt with this issue. The automaker recalled the same vehicles in August 2024 for the same water pump connector problem. At that time, BMW's service bulletin called for installing a splash guard over the connector. However, according to the NHTSA's press release , 10 vehicles that had already received the 2024 repair experienced incidents, prompting BMW to reopen its investigation.
 Advertisement Advertisement Notification letters are expected to go out after December 25, but owners don't have to wait for the mail. On or after that date, owners can visit NHTSA.gov/Recalls and enter their vehicle identification number (VIN) to check whether their car is included. If you have questions, BMW's recall hotline is 800-525-7417.
 BMW has said it will repair affected vehicles free of charge, but the company is still working out the fix. In the meantime, if you own one of these models, keep it parked outside and away from buildings.
